Rashi on Shabbat 33b:10:1.english: I will repair something - In the manner that Jacob did when he was saved from the hand of Esau.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:10:2.english: Whole in his Torah - That he did not forget his learning on account of the toil of the journey.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:10:3.english: Whole in his body - For he was healed from his limp.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:10:4.hebrew: תיקן להם - דברי חן וחנייה. ולי נראה, מויקן את חלקת השדה — לשון תיקון:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:10:4.english: He established for them - [These are] matters of grace [chen] and encampment [ḥanayah, playing on vayichan]. But to me it appears [that it is derived] from “And he bought [vayiken] the parcel of the field” (Genesis 33:19) — an expression of establishing [tikkun].

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:1:1.hebrew: על המעשר - האוכל פירותיו טבלים, והוא במיתה בידי שמים, וזוהי מיתתו מדה במדה — דדרך גרונו נכנס במעיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:1:1.english: For the tithe - One who eats his produce [while it is] untithed (tevel), and he is [liable to] death at the hand of Heaven; and this is his death measure for measure, for through his throat [the food] entered into his innards.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:1.hebrew: לכרם - זה בית המדרש, שיושבין שורות שורות ככרם. כך מפורש בירושלמי בברכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:1.english: To the vineyard - This is the study hall, where they sit in rows upon rows like a vineyard. Thus it is explained in the Yerushalmi in Berakhot.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:3.hebrew: ראש המדברים - במצות המלך, שצוה עליו לדבר תחלה בכל מקום, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:3.english: The head of the speakers - By command of the king, who commanded that he speak first in every place, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:4.hebrew: פה גומר - לשון הרע, והוא בא על כך. לפיכך מתחיל במעיים ומסיים בפה, שהלב מבין לספר לשון הרע ובודה הדברים מלבו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:4.english: The mouth completes - [The utterance of] slander, and it [the affliction] comes on account of this. Therefore, it begins in the intestines and ends in the mouth, for the heart understands to speak slander and fabricates the matters from its heart.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:5.english: The mouth completes - Everything emerges from the throat.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:6.hebrew: דברים טמאים סלקא דעתך - וכי עונשה מיתה? דבשלמא לשון הרע עונשה מיתה, דכתיב (תהילים ק״א:ה׳): "מלשני בסתר רעהו אותו אצמית":
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:6.english: Does it enter your mind [to say] non-kosher food - And is its punishment death? For granted, [with regard to] slander, its punishment is death, as it is written: “Whoever secretly slanders his neighbor, him I will destroy” (Psalms 101:5).

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:7.hebrew: מתוקנין - מעושרים, שהטבל במיתה בידי שמים, כדיליף באלו הן הנשרפים (סנהדרין דף פג.):
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:7.english: Prepared - Tithed; for [eating] untithed produce is [punishable] by death at the hands of Heaven, as is derived in the chapter [entitled] Elu Hen HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 83a).

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:8.hebrew: בעון בטול תורה - דענוש נמי מיתה, כדאמרן: מקרא נדרש לפני פניו, ״למען ירבו ימיכם״ — הא אם לא תלמדו, יתמעטו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:2:8.english: For the sin of dereliction in Torah [study] - For it, too, is punishable by death, as we said: A verse is expounded [with reference to] the verse before the one preceding it, "that your days may be multiplied" (Deuteronomy 11:21) — which implies: but if you do not study, they will be diminished.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:3:1.hebrew: נשים יוכיחו - שאינן מצוות על דברי תורה, דכתיב: "ולמדתם אותם את בניכם" — ולא בנותיכם — ומתות באסכרה. אמר להן: אף הן מבטלות את בעליהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:3:1.english: Women will prove - For they are not commanded regarding words of Torah, as it is written: “And you shall teach them to your sons” — and not your daughters — and [yet] they die of askara. He said to them: They too cause their husbands to neglect [Torah study].

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:3:2.hebrew: תינוקות יוכיחו - שאינן בני לימוד. אמר להן: אף הן בעון שמבטלים את אביהם — להוליכן לחמה ולצונן, ולפייסן באגוזים:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:3:2.english: Children will prove [it] - For they are not capable of study. He said to them: Even they [suffer] for the sin of causing their father to be idle [from Torah study] — to take them into the sun and into the cool, and to appease them with nuts.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:3:3.english: [Children] of the schoolhouse - They neither neglect [Torah study] nor cause [others] to neglect [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:4:1.hebrew: אם לא תדעי לך - לשמור מצותי, צאי לך ובקשי רחמים בזכות עקבי הצאן — אבות הראשונים, שהיו רגלי הצאן וחזוקם; ורעי בזכותן את גדיותיך — תינוקות שלך, שלא יתפשו על משכנות הרועים — רועי הדור ופרנסיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:4:1.english: If you know not - [How] to observe My commandments, go forth and plead for mercy in the merit of the footsteps of the flock — the early Patriarchs, who were the feet of the flock and their support; and in their merit feed your kids — your young children — so that they will not be seized [as collateral] on account of the shepherds’ tents — the shepherds of the generation and its leaders.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:4:2.hebrew: ש"מ אף על לשון הרע - ולא פליג אמעשר, דהא קאמר הכא שהם אוכלין דברים שאינן מתוקנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:4:2.english: Conclude from it: Also for slander - And he does not disagree about [the sin of neglecting] tithes, for behold, he says here that they eat things that are not rectified [i.e., untithed produce].

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:5:1.english: Son of converts - He was the son of a male convert and a female convert.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:5:3.english: Marketplaces - The orderly layout of town marketplaces and their streets.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:5:4.hebrew: וסיפר דבריהם - לתלמידים או לאביו ואמו, ולא להשמיען למלכות, ונשמעו על ידו למלכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:5:4.english: And related their statements - To [his] students or to his father and mother, and not to make them heard to the monarchy, and [yet] through him they were heard by the monarchy.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:5:5.english: Shall be elevated - To be the head of the speakers.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:6:1.hebrew: איברי להו חרובא - לאכול פירותיו, ועינא דמיא לשתות:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:6:1.english: A carob [tree] was created for them - To eat its fruit, and a spring of water to drink.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:6:2.hebrew: בחלא - בחול, שהיו פושטין בגדיהם שלא יבלו, ומכסין ערותן בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:6:2.english: In sand - In sand — for they would remove their clothes so that they would not wear out, and cover their nakedness with sand.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:2.hebrew: ועוסקין בחיי שעה - דאפשר על ידי נכרים, והקב"ה הוא מחלק מזון וריוח לעושי רצונו:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:2.english: And engage in temporal life - For [this] is possible [to be done] through gentiles, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, distributes food and ample sustenance to those who do His will.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:3.hebrew: משפט רשעים בגיהנם י"ב חודש - שנאמר (ישעיהו ס״ו:כ״ג): ״ואשם לא תכבה, והיה מדי חדש בחדשו ומדי שבת בשבתו יבא כל בשר״ — אף הנדונים בו במשמע. מה שבתות למינוי שלהם, אף חדשים למינוי שלהן. והאי ודאי בפושעי גיהנם משתעי, דכתיב לעיל מיניה: ״ויצאו וראו בפגרי האנשים הפושעים בי״. הכי תני לה בסדר עולם (פ"ו):
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:3.english: The judgment of the wicked in Gehenna [lasts] twelve months - As it is stated (Isaiah 66:23): “And their fire shall not be quenched; and it shall come to pass, that from one New Moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh shall come” — even those who are judged in it [Gehenna] are included [in “all flesh”]. Just as Sabbaths are according to their reckoning, so too months are according to their reckoning [i.e., twelve months]. And this [passage] certainly speaks of the sinners of Gehenna, as it is written before it: “And they shall go forth and look upon the carcasses of the men who have rebelled against Me” (Isaiah 66:24). Thus it is taught in Seder Olam (ch. 6).

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:4.hebrew: די לעולם - בעוסקי תורה, אני ואתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:7:4.english: Sufficient for the world - [As for] those who engage in Torah, you and I [suffice].

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:8:1.english: Two bundles - Bundles of myrtle to smell on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:8:2.english: Bundles - Like “the chains of the Pleiades” (Job 38:31).

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:9:2.english: Cracks - Fissures, cracks caused by the sand.

Rashi on Shabbat 33b:9:3.hebrew: וקמצווחו ליה - לר' שמעון, שהדמעות מלוחין ומכאיבין את המכה בתחלתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 33b:9:3.english: And caused him to cry out - To Rabbi Shimon; for tears are salty and cause pain to the wound initially.

Tosafot on Shabbat 33b:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג ר"ת: הלך רבי יהודה בן גרים וסיפר דברים ונשמעו למלכות - ויש ספרים שכתב בהן "יהודה". ואין נראה לרבינו תם; דאמרינן בפרק קמא דמועד קטן (דף ט.): כי הוו מיפטרי ר' יהודה בן גרים ור"ש בן חלפתא מר' שמעון בן יוחי, אמר ליה לבריה: "אנשים הללו אנשי צורה הם, זיל גבייהו דליברכוך" — מכלל דגברא רבה היה. ובסוף שמעתא ל"ג "גל של עצמות" בלשון גנאי, אלא "נח נפשיה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 33b:5:1.english: So reads Rabbeinu Tam: "Rabbi Yehuda ben Gerim went and related statements, and they were heard by the monarchy" - And there are books in which it is written: "Yehuda" [without the title "Rabbi"]. But this does not seem [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for we say in the first chapter of Moed Katan (9a): When Rabbi Yehuda ben Gerim and Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta were taking leave of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, he said to his son: "These men are men of noble form; go to them so that they may bless you" — which implies that he was a great man. And at the end of the sugya, [Rabbeinu Tam] does not read "a heap of bones," which is derogatory phrasing, but rather: "his soul rested."
